findings.evidence: By reading the code (no test exercises this path): `group_size = now.len()` is taken from `batches.remove(0)` before `one_at_a_time` splits off all but one item. batches_for (2834) drops tried items, so the next wave sees the rest of the same group. A plan group of 3 worked serially is therefore recorded as [3, 2, 1] and printed 'groups 3 worked, sizes 3, 2, 1, mean 2.0' when one group of 3 was worked. drain() always calls drain_with(..., true, ...) (2803), and drain_concurrent does the same when workers == 1 (2822). The new tests use 3 workers only. findings.summary: Items with no plan entry are counted as groups of 1.
findings.evidence: batches_for puts each unplanned item in its own singleton batch ahead of the plan groups. The loop records it as a group of size 1, which lowers the mean, but the Report and CHANGELOG describe the record as the item count of each plan group.

The stale "1 to 8" mentions in the design docs are fixed. The Built note and the CHANGELOG entries are present, and every changed file is on the deliverables list. The new tests for the help text, the 16/17 limits, the group sizes and the end-of-run line all pass. fmt and clippy passed in CI. The one CI test failure was a pid-file/process test this change does not touch; it passed when I reran it here, along with the whole athena-cli package, so I judge it a flake. The bug: group sizes are recorded per wave, not per plan group. When the drain runs one job at a time (serial `drain()` or max_concurrency = 1, the default), a single group of 3 is reported as "groups 3 worked, sizes 3, 2, 1, mean 2.0". The tests only use 3 workers, so they miss it. A smaller issue: items with no plan entry are counted as groups of 1. To fix: record a group's size once, when its first wave starts, and add a test with one worker.
